executive_summary.text: In Q1 2026 INFANT saw notable growth in Instagram reach (+65.4% QoQ) and a strong rise in publications (+157.1% QoQ). Email performance improved markedly, with open rates more than doubling QoQ. However, Facebook interactions fell sharply (-38.6% QoQ) and several KPI counts showed declines, indicating mixed momentum across channels.

key_findings.statement: Instagram reach increased to 10,533, up 65.4% from Q4 2025, though the metric aggregates daily reach and may double‑count users.
Facebook interactions dropped to 352, a 38.6% decline from Q4 2025, signalling reduced engagement on that platform.
Publications rose to 36, a 157.1% increase from Q4 2025, reflecting heightened research output.
Email open rate surged to 52.8%, up 124% QoQ, while click‑to‑open fell to 25.9%, indicating higher visibility but lower deeper engagement.

kpi_analysis.interpretation: Poster presentations doubled QoQ to 16, suggesting increased conference activity, though the base is small.
New research staff rose to 9, a 200% increase QoQ, indicating recruitment success with a limited base.
Total current research staff grew to 67 (+6.3% QoQ), showing modest staff expansion.
Registered postgraduate students fell to 29 (-9.4% QoQ), a decline in enrolment.
Funding secured fell to €2 million (-45.9% YoY), a reduction in award income.
Oral presentations decreased to 8 (-11.1% QoQ), indicating fewer speaking slots.

kpis.summary: KPIs show mixed trends: staff growth and publications up, funding and postgraduate enrolment down.

trends.statement: Instagram reach and visits show upward momentum, while Facebook interactions and views decline, indicating platform‑specific dynamics.

cross_dataset.statement: Email open rate improvement coincides with higher Instagram reach, suggesting broader audience activation, though causality is not established.

risks.statement: Sharp decline in Facebook interactions (‑38.6% QoQ) may reduce visibility on that platform.
Funding secured fell to €2 million (‑45.9% YoY), risking financial capacity for research projects.

opportunities.statement: Strong growth in Instagram reach (+65.4% QoQ) offers a channel to amplify research dissemination.
High open‑access share (91.7%) can be leveraged to enhance citation impact and public engagement.

recommendations.recommendation: Invest in targeted content for Instagram to sustain reach growth and convert visits into deeper engagement.
recommendations.reasoning: Instagram metrics are rising while Facebook declines, indicating audience shift.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Maintain audience growth and improve overall digital impact.

recommendations.recommendation: Review Facebook strategy and content mix to address the 38.6% drop in interactions.
recommendations.reasoning: Interaction decline suggests reduced relevance or reach on the platform.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Stabilise engagement and protect platform diversity.

recommendations.recommendation: Seek additional funding sources to offset the 45.9% YoY reduction in secured funding.
recommendations.reasoning: Funding decline may limit research capacity.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Sustain research output and staff recruitment.

data_gaps: Website analytics not connected; post‑level content metrics unavailable; event calendar dates missing; partnership details limited to headline figure.

best_performing.statement: Instagram reach (10,533) and publications (36) showed the strongest positive quarter‑on‑quarter changes.

limitations: All figures were calculated by the dashboard from the sources above. The AI interpreted them but did not calculate any number, and every figure it quotes was checked against the data; any problems found are shown with the report.
Where a period was not fully covered by data, comparisons use the same number of days in each period.
Instagram reach adds up each day's reach, so one account can be counted on several days; it is not the number of unique accounts reached.
Follower figures are new followers gained, not net growth: people who unfollowed are not subtracted.
Changes between periods show association, not cause.
